recap.text: Carl has no measurements for the ramp he wanted, so he builds landmines: metal tubes of hob-lobbers and one stick of hobgoblin dynamite, with plungers made from the Gorgon Marital Aid. The System labels it a Jelly Bomb. He lowers one onto the track with a fishing pole and places a second half a car's length into the tunnel. The train derails, and Carl reaches level 29, with the achievement Locomotive Breath and a Gold Engineering Box.

beats.headline: Landmines, a classic
beats.text: For the first derailment Carl keeps it simple. He wanted a metal ramp to lift the first car off the rails, but he has no measurements, so he goes with a classic: landmines, tire-shaped cross sections of the spiked contact mines of early twentieth-century naval warfare. Each is an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and one hopefully-stable stick of hobgoblin dynamite, its top half scored into triangles for shrapnel. A spike pressed by the train smashes an impact-detonated hob-lobber. The plunger idea came from the cookbook, changed just enough, and he built the plungers from the Gorgon Marital Aid. The System labels it a Jelly Bomb, presumably after a jelly donut. He gets no credit for inventing it.
beats.gist: Carl builds landmines from hob-lobbers, hobgoblin dynamite, and Gorgon Marital Aid plungers; the System calls them Jelly Bombs.

beats.headline: Lowered on a fishing pole
beats.text: According to the Demolitions Workshop menu the device is stable against anything except heavy impact, and Carl watches its status number nervously anyway. It does not lower. With a fishing pole he has cobbled together, he lowers the first one onto the track, as far from the third rail as he can, and places a second half a car's length into the tunnel. Neither has been tested. He is reasonably certain two will be enough to knock the train off the track, and hopes he does not kill the engineer. Or himself.
beats.gist: Carl lowers one Jelly Bomb onto the track with a fishing pole, places a second, and hopes.

beats.headline: Locomotive Breath
beats.text: Even from the top of the stairs the detonation is deafening. Below the platform comes a horrific screeching and crashing, smoke and dust billowing up, and then a second explosion, like a shotgun blast through the tumult. Carl reaches level 29, and the System hands him an achievement, Locomotive Breath, for finally managing to manufacture a train derailment, with the hope that it does not set off some unforeseen domino effect across the rest of the floor. The reward is a Gold Engineering Box. That was ominous, Carl thinks. Out of the tipped engine climbs the ochre line's engineer, Gore-Gore.
beats.gist: Carl reaches level 29 after his Jelly Bomb derails a train, earning Locomotive Breath.

beats.headline: The prototype trigger
beats.text: Carl wants to sandwich a horde of ghouls and monsters between two trains, partly to see whether he gets experience for it. Apart from the landmines that derailed that first train, he has hardly had a chance to use explosives on this floor. The trigger he ties to his bundle of hobgoblin dynamite is a piece of his first landmine prototype: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high to hit the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a stage-three monster. If it misses, the bomb goes off when the train crashes into the other one.
beats.gist: Carl rigs hobgoblin dynamite to a pole trigger, hoping to crush a horde between two trains.
